clue.text: Where one could be at work, away from work cooler!

definitions.text: Where one could be at work

blocks.note: off means away from, as in off the premises
ice is what cools a drink

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be away from their job, somewhere cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses work twice: once inside the definition, once with away from as off (off work). The exclamation hints at a water cooler, an office fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is the workplace where a clerk or manager spends the working day.

clue.text: Opera gig playing musical exercise

indicators.note: musicians playing improvise and rework things, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A singer warms up with scales before an opera booking.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a broken chord, practised by players as a technical drill.

clue.text: Step in road when buggy backed

indicators.note: something buggy is faulty and full of errors, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A parent steps into the road while reversing a pushchair.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface a buggy is a pushchair and backed means reversed; cryptically buggy signals the rearrangement and backed means supported.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise a shop or the arts is to support it, so patronised means supported, as a patron would.

clue.text: Articulate team in the US

blocks.note: to articulate is to state clearly
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: An eloquent sports team plays in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an informal adverb meaning in or towards the United States.

clue.text: Suggestion about start of return journey

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps around a letter
the start of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion
opening letter of return

explanation.surface: Someone offers advice on getting back from a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Little food? That makes one cry

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for little
a pie is an item of food

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of food is so meagre it brings someone to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is an informal name for a sentimental film or book designed to bring on tears.

clue.text: Stir Scottish dish

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for time served in prison, as stir is slang for prison
second meaning: oat breakfast cereal cooked in water or milk

explanation.walkthrough: Stir looks like an instruction for cooking oats, but it is slang for prison; doing porridge is British slang for serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a prison term in British slang and the oatmeal breakfast associated with Scotland.

clue.text: Further belligerent action entertained by US president

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken inside their home, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: Gerald Ford, 38th US president
war is hostile military action

explanation.surface: A US president hosts more warmongering.
explanation.walkthrough: Further reads as an adjective in the surface but is the verb meaning to promote.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a cause is to promote or advance it, the verb sense of further.

clue.text: Action that may be reversed?

indicators.note: the question asks us to notice that turning this word around leaves it unchanged

blocks.note: an act or action

explanation.surface: A decision or act could be undone later.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an act that can be undone; cryptically the word reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an act, so it is a direct synonym for action.

clue.text: Journalist consumed by endless lethargy, wreck

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
something consumed is swallowed, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: torpor is sluggish lethargy; it loses its last letter
ED, short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter is overwhelmed by never-ending sluggishness and falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck or sabotage it, as a torpedo sinks a ship.

clue.text: Train seen going off the rails, seriously

indicators.note: a derailed train is thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Witnesses really did see a train derail.
explanation.definitionFit: In earnest is an idiom meaning sincerely or with serious intent.

clue.text: Piano: one for each musician

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the Roman numeral for one
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: Every member of the band gets a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is someone who plays the bagpipes or pipe, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Push something fragile away from the edge?

blocks.clueFragment: Push something fragile away from the edge?
blocks.note: surface reading: nudging a breakable object to safety on a table

blocks.clueFragment: something fragile away from the edge
blocks.note: setter's reading: the fragile thing is the breakfast item with a shell, and away from the edge means still on the table

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning to urge someone is pictured literally as a breakable shell kept safely on the table rather than off it.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is an idiom meaning to urge or encourage someone, a figurative push.

clue.text: Arrest American, part with shackles

indicators.note: to shackle is to hold captive, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: to spend money is to part with it
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Police detain an American and part of the arrest involves handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a process is to halt it, as to suspend it is to stop it for a time.

clue.text: Inform about a communist agreement that’s fair

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the others

blocks.note: to squeal is to inform on someone to the police
taken as written
red is the usual term for a communist

explanation.surface: Someone tells the authorities about a deal struck with a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A square deal is an idiom for an honest, equitable arrangement.

clue.text: Single number?

blocks.note: surface reading: a lone digit or a number that is just one
setter's reading: a single is a pop record, played on a turntable at a particular speed in revolutions per minute

explanation.walkthrough: Old vinyl singles were played at 45 rpm, so the speed became a name for the record itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-inch vinyl record spinning at that rpm speed was commonly called by the number.

clue.text: This promise kept by irascible fox

blocks.note: cross means bad-tempered
to give one's word is to promise
to fox someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered fox keeps a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: This refers to the very thing the solver is doing; the angry pledge comes first, then the verb for baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is working on exactly this kind of grid, so This points to the puzzle at hand.

clue.text: Spade perhaps gathering up most of box, food container?

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so one word encloses others
most but not all means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a spade is a playing card suit
taken as written
taken as written, shortened by its last letter

explanation.surface: A garden spade scoops up most of a box, perhaps to hold food.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a cabinet, often in a kitchen, where food is stored.

clue.text: Extremism very much on track under extreme characters in Zimbabwe

indicators.note: extreme characters are the ones at each end of the word

blocks.note: first and last letters of Zimbabwe
a lot means very much
RY is short for railway

explanation.surface: Political extremism in Zimbabwe seems firmly on course.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, under places one piece below another, so the Zimbabwe letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealotry is fanatical, uncompromising devotion to a cause, which is a form of extremism.

clue.text: Semi-precious mineral that’s terrible put back in container

indicators.note: put back means turned around, so the word is read from its end
in places the turned word inside the vessel

blocks.note: a pot is a container
dire means terrible

explanation.surface: An ugly gemstone is returned to its box.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a semi-precious form of the mineral olivine.

clue.text: Set up some semi-German system that’s ordered

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used
in a down answer, set up means raised, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: letters running across semi and German

explanation.surface: Someone establishes a partly German orderly arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is an organised system of rule or management.

clue.text: Again supply weapons to attention-grabbing marines?

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of, so one piece is clutched inside another

blocks.note: RM stands for Royal Marines
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Should eye-catching marines be given fresh arms?
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip again with arms, i.e. to resupply with weapons.

clue.text: Country in West Africa, lake also mentioned initially turning up?

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each word
in a down answer, turning up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.clueFragment: in West Africa, lake also mentioned
blocks.note: first letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A West African country and a lake come up in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface is false: Malawi is in south-east Africa, not the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-eastern Africa, so it is a country.

clue.text: Glass fallen, smashed, though not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only a portion of the words is used

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A glass has fallen and broken, though only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is a shaped piece of glass, and glasses are lenses for the eyes.

clue.text: Newspaper perhaps, vital thing

blocks.note: first meaning: a publication that speaks for a group, such as a party's journal
second meaning: a body part such as the heart or liver

explanation.walkthrough: Vital here means essential to life, describing a bodily part rather than something important.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a mouthpiece publication and an internal body part with a vital function.

clue.text: Relative fool

blocks.note: first meaning: grandmother, informally
second meaning: British slang for an idiot, as in to feel a right one

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are informal: a family name for grandmother, and British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a pet name for a grandmother and also British slang for a silly person.

clue.text: Three American points for this in gold leaf, I gathered

indicators.note: fabric that is gathered is bunched and rumpled, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A team wins three points in American football and collects gilded trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football, a kick between the posts during play scores three points.
explanation.definitionFit: A field goal is the kicked score worth three points in American football.

clue.text: Russian dynasty with country in range, dropping back

indicators.note: dropping the back means losing the last letter
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: to range is to rove or wander; its last letter goes
Oman, a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A Russian ruling family retreats with a nation within its territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the imperial house that ruled Russia from 1613 to 1917.

clue.text: Bird has fight after fight

blocks.note: to spar is to box or fight
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A bird gets into one scrap after another.
explanation.walkthrough: After here means placed after: the quarrel follows the boxing bout.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small, common brown songbird.
